description:
FILED s515c (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-11) from the HTTP-Tiny-0.090-0 board census.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs main 973bdb1d; scratch/s515c/pr/iodir5.pl):
    use Symbol;
    sub op { my ($dh, $n) = @_; return opendir($dh, $n) }
    my $g = gensym; op($g, "/etc") or die;
    my @a = readdir($g); print scalar(@a), "\n";      # perl: the entry count   PCL: 0
`opendir($_[0], ...)` works (it aliases the caller's box) and `open` on the same copy works; only opendir.

CAUSE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp %p-opendir-impl stores the `(index . names)` cons with `(setf (p-box-value dh) handle)` when DH is a box -- for a box holding a TYPEGLOB (a glob ref: gensym, \*FH) that overwrites the lexical copy and leaves the glob, which the caller holds, without a dirhandle; %p-resolve-dh has no typeglob arm either.  FIX (one mechanism): a typeglob (bare, or the value of the box) keys *p-dirhandles* by the glob object (the table is EQ) in both %p-opendir-impl and %p-resolve-dh (closedir/rewinddir already go through the resolver).

REACH: core IO::Dir (`new` gensyms and calls IO::Dir::open($dh, ...)) -- every `IO::Dir->new(...)->read` is empty.  HTTP-Tiny-0.090-0: t/Util.pm dir_list feeds 100_get (186 rows), 102_put, 103_delete, 104_post, 110_mirror, 130_redirect, 140_proxy, 150_post_form, 160_cookies, 161_basic_auth, 162_proxy_auth, 170_keepalive, 101_head -- each runs 0 rows ("1..0") from the dist root.

=== DONE (s516a) ===
One key: %p-typeglob-handle-key (the symbol open keys a glob's handle by; its three inline copies in %p-install-fh / %p-forget-fh replaced) through %p-dh-key, used by %p-opendir-impl, %p-resolve-dh (readdir / rewinddir / telldir / seekdir) and %p-closedir-impl.  The reproducer = perl (5 entries); IO::Dir->new(DIR)->read lists.  Guard Pl/t/opendir-01.t (8; rows 1-4, 7-8 fail on main).  Commit 7ef9a9eb (s516a).  The board rows stay behind #1575.
subject: SILENT WRONG: opendir on a COPY of a glob ref (`my ($dh) = @_; opendir($dh, ...)` on a gensym) stores the dirhandle in the copy's box, not the glob -- core IO::Dir->new(DIR)->read returns NOTHING (HTTP-Tiny t/Util.pm dir_list: 100_get.t 186 rows and most of the dist)
